Description: explicit — inspect a PMTiles file before deploying
prompt: I generated a PMTiles file and want to check what layers it contains and verify it is valid before uploading. How?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a step-by-step checklist you can run on your workstation (or in a CI job) to **inspect the layer list** of a PMTiles archive and **verify that the file is structurally sound** before you push it to S3, Cloudflare R2, GitHub Pages, etc.

---

## 1️⃣ Install the official **pmtiles CLI**

The CLI is a single binary (no Node, Go, or Python runtime needed). Pick the version that matches the spec you used when you built the file (v3 is the current stable spec).

| OS | Download command |
|----|------------------|
| macOS (Intel) | `curl -L -o pmtiles https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v3.2.0/pmtiles-darwin-amd64 && chmod +x pmtiles` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `curl -L -o pmtiles https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v3.2.0/pmtiles-darwin-arm64 && chmod +x pmtiles` |
| Linux (amd64) | `curl -L -o pmtiles https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v3.2.0/pmtiles-linux-amd64 && chmod +x pmtiles` |
| Windows | Download `pmtiles-windows-amd64.exe` from the same release page and rename to `pmtiles.exe` (add it to your PATH). |

> **Tip** – If you use Docker you can also run `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data protomaps/go-pmtiles:latest <subcommand> …` instead of installing the binary.

---

## 2️⃣ Quick sanity check – **`show`**

```bash
./pmtiles show my-data.pmtiles
```

What you’ll see (example output):

```
File: my-data.pmtiles
  Type: vector
  Version: 3
  Tile count: 1 254 321
  Bounds: [-180.0000, -85.0511, 180.0000, 85.0511]
  MinZoom: 0
  MaxZoom: 14
  Compression: gzip
  Metadata entries: 7
```

If the command fails with an error like *“invalid header”* or *“unexpected EOF”* the archive is corrupted and you should rebuild it.

---

## 3️⃣ **List the vector layer names** – `show --metadata`

The layer names that you will later reference in a MapLibre style (`"source-layer": "…"` ) live in the JSON metadata under the `vector_layers` array. The plain `show` command only prints a summary, so ask for the full metadata:

```bash
./pmtiles show --metadata my-data.pmtiles
```

Typical JSON fragment (pretty-printed for readability):

```json
{
  "name": "my-data",
  "format": "pbf",
  "bounds": "-180,-85.0511,180,85.0511",
  "minzoom": 0,
  "maxzoom": 14,
  "vector_layers": [
    {
      "id": "water",
      "description": "Water bodies",
      "fields": {
        "class": "String",
        "name": "String"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "roads",
      "description": "All road geometries",
      "fields": {
        "class": "String",
        "type": "String",
        "name": "String"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "buildings",
      "description": "Building footprints",
      "fields": {
        "height": "Number",
        "min_height": "Number"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**What to look for**

| Item | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| `vector_layers` array | Every object’s `id` is the exact string you will use for `"source-layer"` in the style. |
| `minzoom` / `maxzoom` | The archive’s native zoom range. MapLibre will automatically over-zoom beyond `maxzoom` if you reference the source with `url:` (not `tiles:`). |
| `bounds` | Useful for setting `maxbounds` in the map or for splitting archives later. |
| `format` | Should be `"pbf"` for vector, `"png"`/`"jpeg"` for raster, `"terrarium"`/`"mapbox"` for raster-dem. |

If the `vector_layers` array is missing, the file is **not a valid vector PMTiles archive** (the spec requires it). You can still use it for raster, but you’ll need to change the source `type` accordingly.

---

## 4️⃣ **Full structural verification** – `verify`

`verify` walks the internal index, checks offsets, tile counts, and that the header matches the actual data layout. It does **not** decode each tile (that would be far slower), but it catches most file-corruption problems.

```bash
./pmtiles verify my-data.pmtiles
```

Typical success output:

```
✅  Verification passed
   Header OK
   Tile index OK (1 254 321 entries)
   Tile data offsets OK
   Zoom levels OK (0-14)
   Bounds OK
```

If something is wrong you’ll see a red-colored error line, e.g.:

```
❌  Tile index entry #12345 points outside file bounds (offset 9 876 543, length 12 345)
```

In that case you must **re-run the tile generation step** (tippecanoe, Planetiler, etc.) because the archive is broken.

---

## 5️⃣ Optional: **Inspect a single tile** (quick sanity test)

Sometimes you want to be sure the tiles actually contain the geometry you expect. The CLI can extract a tile as raw PBF (or PNG/JPEG for raster) and pipe it to a viewer.

```bash
# Example: get tile z=12, x=657, y=1582
./pmtiles tile my-data.pmtiles 12/657/1582 > tile.pbf
# Then inspect with tippecanoe's tile-join or mapbox/tile-join, or with `vt2geojson`
vt2geojson tile.pbf | jq .
```

If the file is empty or the command errors, the tile may be missing from the archive (e.g. you asked for a zoom level outside the range). Double-check the `minzoom`/`maxzoom` you saw in `show`.

---

## 6️⃣ **Programmatic check (Node / browser)** – using the `pmtiles` library

If you prefer to embed the check in a CI script or a small Node utility, the same library that MapLibre uses can read the header and list layers:

```js
// check-pmtiles.js
import { PMTiles } from "pmtiles";
import { readFile } from "fs/promises";

async function main(file) {
  const data = await readFile(file);
  const archive = await PMTiles.fromArrayBuffer(data.buffer);
  const header = await archive.getHeader();
  console.log("type:", header.tileType);
  console.log("zoom range:", header.minZoom, "–", header.maxZoom);
  console.log("bounds:", header.bounds);
  console.log("layers:");
  const meta = await archive.getMetadata();
  const layers = JSON.parse(meta).vector_layers || [];
  layers.forEach(l => console.log("  -", l.id));
}
main(process.argv[2] ?? "my-data.pmtiles");
```

Run it with `node check-pmtiles.js my-data.pmtiles`. It will throw if the archive is malformed, giving you a programmatic “fail fast” hook for CI pipelines.

---

## 7️⃣ **CORS & Range-request sanity (optional pre-upload test)**

Even a perfectly valid PMTiles file can fail in the browser if the host you plan to use does not return the required headers.

```bash
# 1️⃣ Check that the server returns Accept-Ranges
curl -I -H "Range: bytes=0-0" https://example.com/my-data.pmtiles

# Expected headers (order may vary)
#   Accept-Ranges: bytes
#   Content-Range: bytes 0-0/12345678
#   Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
#   Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range,Accept-Ranges
```

If you see `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` or the `Accept-Ranges` header is missing, the host will not work for MapLibre. Most static hosts (S3, R2, GitHub Pages, Netlify) already send those headers; you only need to add CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`) if you are serving from a different origin than your web page.

---

## 8️⃣ **Putting it all together – a one-liner for CI**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

FILE=$1

# 1️⃣ Show summary (fails on malformed header)
./pmtiles show "$FILE"

# 2️⃣ Verify structure
./pmtiles verify "$FILE"

# 3️⃣ Extract layer list (fail if missing)
LAYERS=$(./pmtiles show --metadata "$FILE" | jq -r '.vector_layers[].id')
if [[ -z "$LAYERS" ]]; then
  echo "❌ No vector_layers found – not a vector PMTiles archive"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ Layers found: $LAYERS"
```

Add this script to your repo’s `package.json` or CI config and run it before the `aws s3 cp …` step. If any command exits non-zero the pipeline stops, preventing a broken archive from being published.

---

## 📚 Quick reference cheat-sheet

| Command | What you get | Typical use |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| `pmtiles show <file>` | Header summary (type, zoom range, bounds, tile count) | Quick sanity check |
| `pmtiles show --metadata <file>` | Full JSON metadata (including `vector_layers`) | Find the exact `source-layer` names |
| `pmtiles verify <file>` | Structural integrity check (offsets, index, zooms) | Guard against corruption |
| `pmtiles tile <file> z/x/y > out.pbf` | Extract a single tile | Spot-check geometry or raster content |
| `pmtiles extract --bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat --minzoom=… --maxzoom=… <src> <dst>` | Create a smaller regional PMTiles | When you need a subset without re-tiling |
| `pmtiles edit --metadata='{"vector_layers":[…]}' <file>` | Overwrite metadata (rare) | Fix a missing `vector_layers` entry (usually easier to regenerate) |

---

### TL;DR

1. **Install** the `pmtiles` binary.  
2. Run `pmtiles show --metadata my.pmtiles` → read the `vector_layers` IDs (these are the strings you’ll use for `"source-layer"`).  
3. Run `pmtiles verify my.pmtiles` → ensures the file isn’t corrupted.  
4. (Optional) Extract a tile with `pmtiles tile …` to double-check content.  
5. If all three steps succeed, you’re safe to upload the file to any static host that supports **HTTP Range** and **CORS**.

Happy mapping! 🚀

---

## 1️⃣ Install the official **pmtiles CLI**

The CLI is a single binary (no npm, no Python, no Java).  
Pick the right build for your OS/arch and put it on your `$PATH`.

| OS | Download link |
|----|---------------|
| macOS (Intel) | <https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v1.12.0/pmtiles-darwin-amd64> |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | <https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v1.12.0/pmtiles-darwin-arm64> |
| Linux (amd64) | <https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v1.12.0/pmtiles-linux-amd64> |
| Windows (amd64) | <https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v1.12.0/pmtiles-windows-amd64.exe> |

```bash
# Example for macOS Intel
curl -L -o pmtiles https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases/download/v1.12.0/pmtiles-darwin-amd64
chmod +x pmtiles
sudo mv pmtiles /usr/local/bin/
```

> **Tip** – The current stable version (as of Oct 2026) is `v1.12.0`. If you already have a version older than `v1.10.0` you’ll miss the `--metadata` flag on `show`, so upgrade.

---

## 2️⃣ Quick sanity-check: `pmtiles verify`

```bash
pmtiles verify my-data.pmtiles
```

*What it does*  

* Checks the file header (magic bytes, version, tile-type, bounds, min/max zoom).  
* Walks the internal index and makes sure every tile offset/length is inside the file and non-overlapping.  
* Verifies the tile count for each zoom level matches the index.  
* Returns **exit code 0** if everything is OK, otherwise prints a short error message and exits with a non-zero code.

**Typical output when the file is fine**

```
✔︎ verified  my-data.pmtiles
  tile type:  vector
  bounds:    -180.0,-85.0511,180.0,85.0511
  zooms:     0-14
  tiles:     1 234 567
  metadata:  3 212 bytes
```

If you see something like `error: tile offset 123456 out of range` you need to rebuild the archive (most often a corrupted conversion step).

---

## 3️⃣ List the **vector layer names** (or raster metadata)

### 3.1 Vector archives – `pmtiles show --metadata`

```bash
pmtiles show --metadata my-data.pmtiles
```

The `--metadata` flag expands the JSON block that lives in the archive’s *metadata* field. In a **vector** PMTiles file you will see a `vector_layers` array that follows the TileJSON 3.0 spec:

```json
{
  "vector_layers": [
    {
      "id": "water",
      "fields": {
        "class": "String",
        "name": "String"
      },
      "description": "Water bodies"
    },
    {
      "id": "roads",
      "fields": {
        "class": "String",
        "type": "String",
        "name": "String"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "buildings",
      "fields": { "height": "Number", "building": "String" }
    }
  ],
  "bounds": "-180,-85.0511,180,85.0511",
  "minzoom": 0,
  "maxzoom": 14,
  "center": [0,0,2],
  "format": "pbf"
}
```

*The `id` values are exactly what you will use in a MapLibre style as `"source-layer"`*:

```json
{
  "id": "water-fill",
  "type": "fill",
  "source": "myPmtiles",
  "source-layer": "water",
  "paint": { "fill-color": "#a0c8f0" }
}
```

### 3.2 Raster or raster-DEM archives

Raster PMTiles do **not** have a `vector_layers` array. Instead you’ll see keys like:

```json
{
  "format": "png",
  "bounds": "-180,-85.0511,180,85.0511",
  "minzoom": 0,
  "maxzoom": 12,
  "center": [0,0,2],
  "encoding": "terrarium"   // only for raster-dem
}
```

For raster sources you don’t need a `source-layer` – the whole file is the source.

---

## 4️⃣ Optional: Peek at a single tile (helps confirm the geometry/encoding)

```bash
# Grab tile z=10, x=512, y=384 and write it to a file
pmtiles tile my-data.pmtiles 10/512/384 > tile.pbf
# For raster (png) you could open it with any image viewer:
pmtiles tile my-data.pmtiles 12/2048/1024 > tile.png
```

*Why you might do this*  

* Verify that the tile actually contains data (non-empty file size).  
* For vector tiles you can pipe the result through `vt2geojson` or `mapbox-vector-tile` to inspect the feature properties.  
* For raster-DEM you can open the PNG and check that the elevation encoding (Terrarium or Mapbox) looks plausible.

---

## 5️⃣ Putting it all together – a one-liner script

If you want a quick “all-clear” report you can combine the two commands:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

FILE=$1

echo "=== Verifying $FILE ==="
pmtiles verify "$FILE"

echo "=== Metadata (layer list) ==="
pmtiles show --metadata "$FILE" | jq '.vector_layers[].id'   # jq is optional
```

Running `./check-pmtiles.sh my-data.pmtiles` will exit with a non-zero status if verification fails, and it will print each vector layer name on its own line.

---

## 6️⃣ Common pitfalls & how to fix them

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `pmtiles verify` reports “tile offset … out of range” | The file was truncated (e.g. upload interrupted) or the conversion step crashed. | Re-run the conversion (`pmtiles convert …` or the original tippecanoe/planetiler command). |
| `pmtiles show --metadata` prints `<object, use --metadata to view full JSON metadata>` and no `vector_layers` | You omitted `--metadata`. The plain `show` only prints scalar fields. | Add `--metadata`. |
| No `vector_layers` array appears even though you expect vector data | The archive is **raster** (or you generated MBTiles → PMTiles without preserving metadata). | Regenerate with a vector-tile tool (tippecanoe `-o out.pmtiles` or planetiler). |
| MapLibre shows a blank map after you add the source | The file is valid but the style is referencing a non-existent `source-layer`. | Double-check the `id` values from `vector_layers` and use them verbatim in `"source-layer"` fields. |
| CORS error in the browser (`No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header`) | Your static host isn’t sending CORS headers for range requests. | Configure the bucket (S3 → “CORS configuration”) or CDN to return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (or your domain) and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Range`. |
| Tiles load but are always empty at high zooms | The archive’s `maxzoom` is lower than the map’s zoom. | Either (a) generate higher-zoom tiles, or (b) let MapLibre over-zoom by using `url:` (not `tiles:`) – the protocol will automatically repeat the highest-zoom tiles. |

---

## 7️⃣ Quick cheat-sheet

| Command | What you get |
|---------|--------------|
| `pmtiles verify file.pmtiles` | Pass/fail + basic header info |
| `pmtiles show file.pmtiles` | Human-readable summary (bounds, zooms, tile count) |
| `pmtiles show --metadata file.pmtiles` | Full JSON metadata – **vector_layers** list for vector archives |
| `pmtiles extract -b <bbox> -z <zmin>-<zmax> file.pmtiles out.pmtiles` | Sub-set of the original (useful for region-only uploads) |
| `pmtiles tile file.pmtiles <z>/<x>/<y> > tile.ext` | Dump a single tile to disk for inspection |

---

## 8️⃣ Next step – upload & use in MapLibre

Once `verify` passes and you’ve confirmed the layer names, you can:

1. **Upload** the file to your static host (S3, R2, GitHub Pages, Netlify, etc.).  
   *Make sure the bucket serves `Accept-Ranges: bytes` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.*  
2. **Add the PMTiles protocol** in your app (see the skill’s “MapLibre Integration” section).  
3. **Reference the source** with `url: 'pmtiles://https://<host>/<file>.pmtiles'`.  
4. **Add style layers** using the `source-layer` names you just saw.

That’s it – you now have a validated, inspected PMTiles archive ready for a completely server-less MapLibre map! 🚀

|---------|--------------|-----|
| `pmtiles verify` returns *“tile offset … exceeds file size”* | File was truncated during copy/upload. | Re-upload the file with a tool that preserves binary integrity (e.g. `aws s3 cp`, `rclone copy`, or Git LFS). |
| `pmtiles show --metadata` prints `vector_layers: <object, use --metadata to view full JSON metadata>` and you see no `id`s | You ran plain `pmtiles show` (without `--metadata`). | Use the `--metadata` flag; the layer list lives there. |
| MapLibre shows **blank vector tiles** at zoom levels that exist in the archive | You used `tiles: ['pmtiles://…/{z}/{x}/{y}']` instead of `url:`. | Switch to `url:` so the protocol can read the archive’s `maxzoom` and over-zoom correctly. |
| Browser console shows **CORS error** when fetching the .pmtiles file | Host does not send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` or `Accept-Ranges`. | Add those headers on the bucket/object (S3 → “CORS configuration”, Cloudflare R2 → “CORS” tab). |
| `vector_layers` array is missing | The generator didn’t write TileJSON metadata (common with raw MBTiles → PMTiles conversion). | Regenerate the source with a tool that writes metadata (`tippecanoe --layer=…`, `planetiler --layers=…`) or add it manually with `pmtiles edit --metadata='{"vector_layers":[…]}'`. |
| Tile size is huge (several MB) | The whole archive was gzip-compressed **twice** by the static host (e.g., CloudFront + `Content-Encoding: gzip`). | Disable automatic gzip on the host for `.pmtiles` files; the format already stores each tile compressed. |

---

## 7️⃣ TL;DR – One-liner checklist

```bash
# 1️⃣ Verify structure
pmtiles verify my-data.pmtiles && echo "✅ OK"

# 2️⃣ List layers (requires jq)
pmtiles show my-data.pmtiles --metadata |
  jq -r '.vector_layers[].id'   # prints each layer name on its own line
```

If both commands succeed, you’re ready to upload and use the file in MapLibre.

Now you can confidently push the `.pmtiles` file to any static bucket, register the `pmtiles://` protocol once in your app, and reference the layers you just listed in your style. Happy mapping!
